blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Multimodal medical AI requires a common visual interface for encoding heterogeneous imaging evidence for patient condition modeling. However, existing medical visual tokenizers are often tied to a specific dimension and imaging modality, forcing multimodal systems to rely on fragmented and poorly reusable representations. We introduce MedVTok, a general-purpose visual tokenizer that maps 2D images and 3D volumes from diverse imaging modalities into a unified token space. Building such a tokenizer poses two key challenges: preserving anatomical structure across dimensions and capturing clinical semantics across modalities. To this end, MedVTok introduces (i) slice differential regularization, which explicitly models inter-slice anatomical coherence missing in previous per-pixel/per-voxel supervision, and (ii) multi-expert representation alignment, which integrates knowledge from multiple medical expert encoders while retaining modality-specific complementary knowledge. Trained on 28M images and 70K volumes across 9 imaging modalities, MedVTok supports classification, retrieval, segmentation, synthesis, visual question answering, and medical report generation through a single tokenizer. Across 24 benchmarks, MedVTok achieves state-of-the-art performance, demonstrating a scalable token interface that unifies medical image dimension, modality, and task usage.
blocks.zh: 多式联运医学AI需要一种常见的视觉接口来编码患者状况模型的多相成像证据. 然而,现有的医疗视觉表示器往往与特定的维度和成像模式相联,迫使多式系统依赖零碎和难以再使用的表示。 我们引入了MedVTok,一种通用的视觉示意器,将2D图像和3D卷从不同的成像模式映射到一个统一的示意空间. 建立这样一个示意器提出了两个关键的挑战:在维度上保持解剖结构,在模式上捕捉临床语义。 为此,MedVTok引入了(一)切分分法规范化,它明确模拟了以往每像素/每伏克赛尔监督中缺失的切片间解剖一致性,并(二)多专家代表协调,将来自多位医学专家编码器的知识相融合,同时保留特定模式的补充知识. MeDVTok对28M图像和70K卷进行了9个成像模式的培训,支持分类、检索、分解、合成、视觉问题回答,并通过单一的示意剂生成医疗报告。 在24个基准中,MedVTok实现了最先进的性能,展示了一个可伸缩的符号界面,统一了医疗图像的维度、模式和任务使用。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Multimodal medical AI aims to integrate heterogeneous patient evidence, including laboratory measurements, longitudinal records, and medical images, to form a holistic understanding of a patient’s condition.
As the field shifts from isolated task-specific models toward generalist multimodal systems [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] , a central requirement is a shared interface through which diverse clinical evidence can be encoded, transferred, and reused across tasks .
Among these evidence sources, medical images are particularly rich and high-dimensional, capturing anatomical structures, pathological findings, and disease progression.
Visual tokenization therefore serves as a critical front end that converts raw imaging data into compact visual tokens compatible with multimodal models.
blocks.zh:
多式医疗AI旨在整合各种患者证据,包括实验室测量、纵向记录和医疗图像,以形成对患者状况的整体理解。
随着实地工作从孤立的任务模式转向通用的多模式系统[1、2、3],一个核心要求是共享接口,通过这一接口,可以将各种临床证据编码、传输和重复用于不同的任务。
在这些证据来源中,医疗图像特别丰富和高维,能捕捉解剖结构,病理发现和疾病发展.
因此,可视化是将原始成像数据转换成与多模式相容的紧凑可视化标志的关键前端。

blocks.en:
However, medical imaging data are highly heterogeneous across both modality and dimension, including 2D images such as dermoscopic images, color fundus photographs (CFP) and histopathology patches, as well as 3D volumes such as computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
These data differ in acquisition protocol, anatomical coverage, and diagnostic content.
Existing medical visual tokenizers are often tied to a specific modality and dimension, producing fragmented representations that are difficult to reuse in a multimodal system.
Consequently, downstream models must absorb much of the burden of modality adaptation and cross-modality representation learning [ 4 ] .
A general-purpose medical visual tokenizer should instead provide a single token interface across modalities while natively supporting both 2D images and 3D volumes.
blocks.zh:
然而,医疗成像数据在方式和维度上差异很大,包括二维图像,如皮肤图像、彩色花花相片(CFP)和组织病理学补丁等,以及三维卷,如计算成像和磁共振成像(MRI)。
这些数据在获取协议、解剖覆盖和诊断内容方面各不相同。
现有的医疗视觉显示器往往与特定的模式和维度挂钩,产生零碎的表达方式,在多式联运系统中难以再利用。
因此,下游模式必须承担许多适应模式和跨模式代表性学习的负担[4]。
通用医疗视觉显示器应提供一种跨模式的单一信号接口,同时在本土上支持2D图像和3D卷。

blocks.en:
Building such a tokenizer poses two key challenges. (i) Preserving structural fidelity across dimensions. Unlike 2D images, 3D scans present volumetric continuity, where organs, vessels, lesions, and tissue boundaries extend across adjacent slices.
Existing tokenizers often specialize in either 2D or 3D settings [ 5 , 6 ] , or are optimized for local appearance fidelity or per-pixel/per-voxel reconstruction [ 7 , 8 ] , failing to encode inter-slice structure. (ii) Capturing multimodal semantics across modalities. Different modalities may describe related clinical concepts while exposing distinct evidence, e.g. , histopathology reveals cellular and tissue-level morphology, whereas CT and MRI capture organ-level anatomy.
Existing semantic alignment strategies typically learn representations of different imaging modalities from a single pretrained semantic encoder [ 9 , 10 , 6 , 11 ] , which may underrepresent modality-specific semantics outside that encoder’s representation space.
blocks.zh:
建立这样一个标识器提出了两个关键的挑战。 (一) 保持不同层面的结构忠诚。 与2D图像不同,3D扫描呈现出体积连续性,器官,器皿,损伤,组织边界会跨越相邻切片.
已存在的活化剂往往专门用于2D或3D设置[5,6],或被优化为局部外观忠实或每像素/每伏克塞尔重建[7,8],未能将相切结构编码. (二) 掌握跨模式的多式语义。 不同的模式可以描述相关的临床概念,同时暴露出不同的证据,例如:组织病理学揭示出细胞和组织一级形态,而CT和MRI则捕捉出器官一级解剖学.
现有的语义对接策略通常从一个预先训练过的语义编码器[9, 10, 6, 11] 中学习不同成像模式的表达,这些语义可能低于该编码器的表示空间以外的特定模式语义.

blocks.en:
In this paper, we introduce MedVTok, a general-purpose medical visual tokenizer that maps heterogeneous 2D images and 3D volumes from diverse imaging modalities into a unified token space.
To preserve structural fidelity across dimensions, MedVTok introduces Slice Differential Regularization (SliDR) in addition to per-pixel/per-voxel supervision, which explicitly models inter-slice volumetric continuity.
To capture clinical semantics across modalities, MedVTok proposes Multi-Expert Representation Alignment (MERA), which builds a shared representation space integrating knowledge from multiple modality-specialized experts instead of a single one, while retaining complementary semantics in each expert’s representation space.
Together, they enable MedVTok to produce visual tokens that preserve structural fidelity and encode multimodal clinical semantics.

为了保持结构上跨维的忠心,MedVTok除了每个像素/每伏克赛尔监督外,还引入了Slicse differental regularation(SliDR),它明确模拟了Slices间体积连续性.
为了捕捉跨模式的临床语义,MedVTok提出了多专家代表对接(MERA),它建立了一个共享代表空间,将来自多种模式专家的知识融合起来,而不是一个单一的,同时保留每个专家代表空间中的互补语义.
它们共同使MedVTok能够生产出能保存结构忠诚并编码多模式临床语义的视觉符号.

blocks.en:
To train and evaluate MedVTok at scale, we curate a large-scale medical imaging corpus spanning 9 modalities, with over 28M 2D images and 70K 3D volumes.
We assess MedVTok across 6 task types: classification, segmentation, retrieval, synthesis, visual question answering, and medical report generation, covering broad utility across 24 benchmarks.
Our results show that MedVTok achieves state-of-the-art performance, demonstrating the value of a scalable token interface that unifies medical image dimension, modality, and downstream task usage.

为了大规模地训练和评估MedVTok,我们研究了一个涵盖9种模式的大规模医疗成像仪,其图像超过28M 二维和70K 三维卷。
我们评估了MedVTok的6个任务类型:分类、分解、检索、综合、视觉问答和医疗报告生成,涵盖24个基准的广泛用途。
我们的结果显示,MedVTok实现了最先进的性能,展示了一个可伸缩的符号界面的价值,它统一了医疗图像的维度、模式和下游任务使用。

blocks.en: Contributions. Our main contributions are as follows. (i) We introduce MedVTok, a general-purpose medical visual tokenizer that provides a shared token interface across diverse imaging modalities and natively supports both 2D images and 3D volumes. (ii) We propose a multi-level supervision strategy that combines slice differential regularization for inter-slice continuity with multi-expert representation alignment for cross-modality clinical semantics. (iii) We curate a large-scale medical imaging corpus and conduct comprehensive evaluations across 24 benchmarks, demonstrating the broad utility of MedVTok across classification, segmentation, retrieval, synthesis, visual question answering, and medical report generation.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Visual tokenizers convert images into compact tokens while preserving structural fidelity [ 12 , 7 ] .
Recent tokenizers [ 13 , 9 ] further explore how a single tokenizer can handle heterogeneous visual formats such as images and videos.
In medical imaging, however, tokenizers are commonly tied to specific input dimensionalities [ 5 , 6 ] . A few works have explored adaptation to different dimensionalities by pooling 3D weights into 2D [ 8 ] or by duplicating 2D images to fit a 3D model [ 14 ] . While these approaches can handle 2D and 3D inputs simultaneously, they do not consider the respective properties of each dimensionality, e.g. , through-plane anatomical continuity in volumes, and thus cannot fully preserve structural fidelity across input forms.
In contrast, MedVTok introduces Slice Differential Regularization to explicitly preserve anatomical continuity in volumetric data, and provides a unified 2D–3D token interface via dimension-agnostic patchification.

blocks.en:
Medical image representation learning has produced both broad biomedical encoders and modality-specialized expert models.
General medical encoders [ 15 , 16 , 17 , 18 , 19 ] learn transferable representations from large-scale biomedical data, offering broad coverage across medical domains but potentially missing specialty-specific cues.
Meanwhile, specialized encoders capture finer clinical semantics within individual imaging modalities or specialties [ 20 , 21 , 22 , 23 , 24 , 14 , 25 , 26 ] , yet remain isolated in different representation spaces.
Existing tokenizers [ 5 , 6 ] have only partially captured these different semantics, e.g. , MedITok [ 6 ] aligns its representations with those of a single semantic encoder [ 15 ] , thereby inheriting the single-expert bias and limiting the learning of complementary knowledge across modalities.
MedVTok instead uses Multi-Expert Representation Alignment to integrate knowledge from multiple medical experts into a single token space, while retaining modality-specific semantics.

同时,专业编码器在单个成像模式或专业内捕捉更精细的临床语义[20,21,22,23,24,14,25,26],但仍被隔离在不同的代表空间.
现有的符号 [5,6] 仅部分地捕捉了这些不同的语义,例如: Meditok [6] 将其表述与单一语义编码器的表述相统一 [15],从而继承了单一专家的偏差并限制了跨模式学习互补知识.

blocks.en: 3.2 Slice Differential Regularization
blocks.zh: 3.2 切片不同规范化

blocks.en:
In tomographic volumes such as CT and MRI scans, adjacent slices share strong anatomical context: organs span continuously across the depth axis, and their boundaries shift gradually from slice to slice.
Per-voxel reconstruction losses like ℓ 1 \ell_{1} can produce outputs that are individually accurate yet exhibit through-plane discontinuities, compromising diagnostic utility.
We address this with the Slice Differential Regularization , which operates on inter-slice continuity rather than individual voxels.

blocks.en: 3.3 Multi-Expert Representation Alignment
blocks.zh: 3.3 多专家代表对接

blocks.en:
Apart from structural fidelity, a unified medical visual tokenizer should also encode high-level clinical semantics.
Achieving this across the full breadth of medical imaging is challenging as different modalities embed distinct knowledge.
Aligning to a single expert [ 15 , 6 ] constrains the tokenizer to inherit a single semantic geometry, which may underrepresent modalities outside the expert’s training distribution.
We therefore propose Multi-Expert Representation Alignment (MERA), which uses a panel of pretrained modality-specific encoders as semantic experts . MERA involves two objectives: (i) shared-space contrastive alignment, which jointly aligns representations from multiple modality experts into a shared space, and (ii) expert-space complementary alignment, which preserves complementary information in each modality expert’s representation space.

blocks.en: 4.2 Evaluation on Downstream Tasks
blocks.zh: 4.2 对下游任务的评价

blocks.en: We compare MedVTok with both medical-domain tokenizers [ 6 , 5 , 8 ] and general-domain ones [ 29 , 4 , 32 , 10 , 9 ] . We first evaluate token fidelity of different tokenizers via autoencoding reconstruction, and then evaluate token representation quality on 6 downstream tasks: image classification, image-to-image retrieval, image segmentation, image synthesis, visual question answering (VQA), and medical report generation. All evaluations use a frozen tokenizer and focus on the quality of the encoded tokens rather than building task-specific models (§ C.2 ).

We assess token fidelity by how well the tokenizer reconstructs input data from its encoded tokens, reporting PSNR and SSIM between the input and the reconstructed data.
Table 1 reports 2D reconstruction quality. MedVTok ranks first on all nine modalities in both PSNR and SSIM. The improvement is most notable in challenging domains such as pathology, where other tokenizers suffer from limited training diversity. Medical-domain tokenizers (MedITok, MedVAE) and general-domain ones (TokenFlow, UniTok, MingTok) lag significantly behind, confirming that medical images benefit from specialized architectures and large-scale multimodal training. Fig. 3 visualizes the reconstruction error maps of the competing methods and the reconstructed images produced by MedVTok.
The last two columns of Table 1 report native 3D reconstruction. MedVTok achieves the best PSNR and SSIM on both MRI and CT volumes by a large margin over PUMIT and MedVAE. The strong 3D performance suggests that our unified 2D–3D training paradigm effectively transfers learned representations to volumetric data. Please see § C.2 for qualitative comparisons.

blocks.en:
We follow Siméoni et al. [ 55 ] and adopt a linear segmentation protocol to evaluate the representation quality for image segmentation. Specifically, a single linear segmentation head is trained with a cross-entropy loss on top of the frozen patch tokens produced by each tokenizer, with learning rates searched over { 10 − 2 , 10 − 3 , 10 − 4 } \{10^{-2},10^{-3},10^{-4}\} . For each tokenizer, the best-performing head on the validation set is selected for evaluation.
Results are presented in Table 3 . MedVTok achieves the best average Dice score, outperforming all baselines including semantic encoders. This task reveals a clear hierarchy: although general autoencoding tokenizers ( e.g. , SDVAE, PUMIT) can embed rich low-level details into the latent space, their high-level semantics are not activated, resulting in low segmentation performance. Semantic encoders provide explicit visual semantics and significantly outperform the autoencoding tokenizers. Unified tokenizers (MedITok, MedVTok) encode both fine-grained spatial information and high-level semantics, enjoying the benefits of both and improving dense prediction. Please see § C.2 for qualitative comparisons.

blocks.en:
We evaluate how the tokenizer influences text-conditioned medical image synthesis within a latent diffusion [ 29 ] framework. A UNet denoising backbone is trained from scratch in each tokenizer’s latent space while keeping both the tokenizer and the text encoder frozen. This design isolates the effect of the tokenizer: the architecture, noise scheduler, optimizer, and training data are held constant across experiments.
Training uses 70K image–text pairs spanning seven imaging modalities.
We report the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) [ 56 , 57 ] in Table 4 ; lower FID indicates higher fidelity.
MedVTok achieves the highest image synthesis quality with the best average FID, outperforming both specialized tokenizers (PUMIT, MedVAE) and the previous unified tokenizer (MedITok), as shown in Fig. 4 .
PUMIT and MedVAE consistently underperform, confirming that synthesis quality depends not only on reconstruction fidelity but also on a well-structured, semantically meaningful latent space that facilitates the diffusion model’s learning.

Evaluation on generating free-text radiology reports from 3D volumes is similar to VQA, incorporating each frozen tokenizer into the LaMed framework [ 59 ] and training the connector and LLM to generate region-specific findings for three anatomical regions (abdomen, chest, and pelvis).
We report BLEU-2, RaTEScore [ 60 ] (entity-level NER-based evaluation), and GREEN [ 61 ] (clinically aware error detection via an LLM judge).
Table 6 presents the report generation results. MedVTok achieves the best scores on all metrics. The improvement is consistent across anatomical regions, with particularly strong gains in the pelvic region, which is the most challenging due to its complex anatomy and longer reference reports. Compared with MedITok, MedVTok shows meaningful improvements on clinically aware metrics (GREEN: 0.413 vs. 0.386), suggesting that our tokenizer encodes diagnostically relevant information that translates into more accurate clinical language generation. Additional results are provided in § C.2 .

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We present MedVTok, a general-purpose medical visual tokenizer that encodes both 2D images and 3D volumes into a shared representational space through a single transformer architecture. Two complementary supervision mechanisms shape this space at different levels: Slice Differential Regularization preserves inter-slice fidelity that per-voxel supervision misses, and Multi-Expert Representation Alignment injects modality-specific clinical semantics from a panel of experts without requiring paired annotations. MedVTok achieves state-of-the-art results across reconstruction and six downstream tasks, ranging from pixel-level fidelity to report generation, demonstrating that structural fidelity and semantic richness can be jointly optimized within a single tokenizer.
blocks.zh: 我们提出MedVTok,一种通用的医学视觉符号,通过单一的变压器架构将2D图像和3D卷编码成一个共享的代表空间. 有两个互补的监督机制在不同的层面上决定了这一空间: 切片差异规范化保留了每伏克赛尔监督缺失的切片间忠诚,多专家代表对接从一个专家小组注入特定模式的临床语义,不需要配对说明. MedVTok在重建过程中和下游的6个任务中实现了最先进的成果,从像素级忠诚到报告生成,表明结构忠诚和语义丰富可以在一个单一的活化器内共同优化.

blocks.en:
We acknowledge several limitations. First, the training data focus on common imaging modalities at present. Other imaging modalities, clinical photos, or illustrations in medical publications remain unexplored. Incorporating these would enhance generalization to non-standard visual inputs encountered in real-world clinical workflows.
Second, while MERA uses frozen expert encoders, jointly fine-tuning selected experts or incorporating new ones could further improve domain coverage when the computational budget allows.
We hope MedVTok will serve as a useful building block for scalable multimodal medical AI systems that enable patient-level modeling across heterogeneous imaging evidence and clinical tasks.
blocks.zh:
我们承认若干限制。 首先,培训数据目前侧重于共同的成像模式。 其他成像方式,临床相片,或医学出版物中的插图仍然没有得到探讨. 纳入这些内容,将促进在现实世界临床工作流程中遇到的非标准视觉投入的通俗化。
第二,虽然MERA使用被冻结的专家编码器,但如果计算预算允许,联合微调选定的专家或纳入新的专家,可以进一步提高域覆盖范围。
我们希望,MedVTok将成为可扩展的多模式医疗AI系统的有用组成部分,能够使患者一级模型能够涵盖各种成像证据和临床任务。

blocks.en: MedITok [ 6 ] combines reconstruction and semantic alignment for 2D medical images. AToken [ 9 ] provides a unified tokenizer for general-domain images, videos, and 3D assets. SAMTok [ 62 ] and HiMTok [ 63 ] encode segmentation masks as compact token sequences for multimodal language models. MedVTok focuses on a shared representation for medical images and volumes, combining depth-wise reconstruction regularization with semantic supervision from modality-specific experts.

The encoder and decoder of MedVTok each consist of 27 transformer blocks with a hidden dimension of d = 1152 d=1152 . The encoder is initialized from SigLIP2-SO400M-patch16-NaFlex [ 28 ] , while other components are trained from scratch. The patch size is P t × P h × P w P_{t}{\times}P_{h}{\times}P_{w} , where P t = 4 P_{t}=4 is the depth patch size for 3D volumes and P h = 16 , P w = 16 P_{h}=16,P_{w}=16 are the spatial patch sizes for both 2D images and 3D volumes. Rotary position embeddings (RoPE) [ 27 ] are derived from 3D patch coordinates ( z , x , y ) (z,x,y) .
Before the decoder, each encoded d d -dimensional token embedding is projected to a 96-dimensional output, which is split into mean and log-variance for a diagonal Gaussian posterior, yielding latent codes of dimension d z = 48 d_{z}=48 .

blocks.en: All patches from a batch are concatenated into a single flat sequence of shape [ N , 3072 ] [N,3072] , where N N is the total number of patches across the batch. This eliminates dense padding entirely and achieves 𝒪 ⁡ ( N ) \mathcal{O}(N) memory regardless of resolution heterogeneity. Each patch is associated with a coordinate vector ( b , z , x , y ) (b,z,x,y) encoding the batch index, depth position, and spatial position, together with a list of per-sample sequence lengths that enables 𝒪 ⁡ ( 1 ) \mathcal{O}(1) batch-wise slicing. Because the representation has no global spatial grid, a single batch can freely mix different spatial resolutions ( e.g. , 256 × 256 256{\times}256 and 512 × 512 512{\times}512 ), different depths ( e.g. , 16 and 64 slices), and 2D images with 3D volumes simultaneously.

We curate the training set from publicly available medical imaging repositories.
Before quality filtering, we impose minimum dataset size thresholds: only 2D datasets containing at least 9,000 images and 3D datasets containing at least 180 volumes are included. This criterion serves two purposes. First, it prevents commonly used small-scale benchmark datasets from entering the training pool, thereby preserving their integrity for downstream evaluation. Second, it avoids highly fragmented data sources that contribute minimal training signal relative to the overhead of integration.

blocks.en:
We use autoencoding reconstruction as a proxy task to evaluate token fidelity: each input is encoded and decoded by the frozen tokenizer, and we measure how faithfully the tokens preserve the original signal.
For 2D images, evaluation is performed at 512 × 512 512{\times}512 resolution. We report PSNR and SSIM between the input and reconstructed images.
For 3D volumes, we evaluate on CT and MRI using two datasets. CT intensities are clipped to [ − 1000 , 1000 ] [-1000,1000] HU; MRI intensities are clipped at the 0.5th and 99.5th percentiles per volume. PSNR and SSIM are computed at the volume level.
Only models with native 3D support (PUMIT, MedVAE, AToken, MedVTok) are included in the 3D evaluation.
blocks.zh:
我们使用自动编码重建作为评价象征忠诚的代理任务:每个输入由被冻结的活化器编码并解码,我们测量这些活化器如何忠实地保存了原始信号.
对于2D图像,评价以512×512 512\times}512分辨率进行. 我们报告PSNR和SSIM在输入和重构图像之间.
对于3D卷,我们使用两个数据集对CT和核磁共振进行评估. CT强度被剪至 [−1000, 1000] [-1000 1100]. HU;磁共振强度以每卷0.5分之和99.5分之之被剪接. PSNR和SSIM按体积计算。
只有具有本土3D支持的模型(PUMIT, MeDVAE, AToken, MeDVTok)被纳入了3D评价.

blocks.en: We adopt a k k -nearest neighbor ( k k -NN) protocol on frozen features extracted from the CLS token (or equivalent global representation) of each tokenizer. For tokenizers that do not output such a representation ( e.g. , SDVAE), we concatenate all features along the channel dimension. The feature vectors are L 2 L_{2} -normalized, and classification is performed via softmax-weighted voting over the k k nearest neighbors using cosine similarity with a temperature of T = 0.07 T=0.07 . We sweep k ∈ { 10 , 20 , 100 , 200 } k\in\{10,20,100,200\} on the validation set and report the best accuracy for each model. Image resolution is controlled at 256 × 256 256{\times}256 when possible.

blocks.en: We evaluate image-to-image retrieval using the same frozen features and benchmarks as classification. The training split of each dataset serves as the gallery, and the test split provides the queries. For each query, we compute the cosine similarity between its L 2 L_{2} -normalized feature vector and all gallery features, rank the gallery by descending similarity, and report Recall@1 (the fraction of queries whose top-retrieved image shares the same label). Image resolution is controlled at 256 × 256 256{\times}256 when possible, consistent with the classification setup.

blocks.en:
We evaluate the quality of frozen patch tokens for dense prediction by training a lightweight linear segmentation head on top of each tokenizer’s output, following the protocol of Siméoni et al. [ 55 ] . The segmentation head consists of a batch normalization layer followed by a 1 × 1 1{\times}1 convolution. For each tokenizer, we train separate heads under identical settings and select the best-performing one by validation Dice score.
Training runs for 50 epochs with AdamW (no weight decay), a batch size of 32, cross-entropy loss, and learning rates searched over { 10 − 2 , 10 − 3 , 10 − 4 } \{10^{-2},10^{-3},10^{-4}\} . Image resolution is controlled at 256 × 256 256{\times}256 when possible. We report the overall Dice score over segmentation classes. Table 9 further reports Hausdorff Distance at the 95th percentile (HD95), where MedVTok still leads in terms of average performance across modalities.

blocks.en: We evaluate how the quality of a tokenizer’s latent space influences text-conditioned medical image synthesis. Each frozen tokenizer is integrated into a latent diffusion framework [ 29 ] as the only variable: a UNet denoising backbone following the Stable Diffusion v1.4 architecture is randomly initialized for each tokenizer (with input/output channels adapted to match the latent dimensionality), and a frozen CLIP-based text encoder provides conditioning. We train separate diffusion models per tokenizer using identical data, architecture, and hyperparameters, ensuring that differences in generation quality are attributable solely to the tokenizer.
blocks.zh: 我们评价一个示意器的潜在空间的质量如何影响文字条件的医疗图像合成。 每个被冻结的活化剂被集成到潜在扩散框架[29]中,作为唯一的可变因素:对每个活化剂随机初始化了稳定散化v1.4架构后UNet去诺化的主干线(其中输入/输出通道被调整以与潜在维度相匹配),而基于被冻结的CLIP的文本编码器提供条件. 我们使用相同的数据、架构和超参数,每个标定器培训单独的传播模型,确保生成质量的差异完全归因于标定器。

blocks.en:
Training uses 70,000 images from GMAI-VL-5.5M [ 1 ] spanning seven imaging modalities (10,000 images each). The noise scheduler is DDPM with 1,000 timesteps, a scaled-linear beta schedule, and ϵ \epsilon -prediction parameterization. The model is trained with an effective batch size of 256, the AdamW optimizer, a constant learning rate with 5% linear warmup, and classifier-free guidance dropout of 10%.
Note that the purpose of this experiment is to compare the generative suitability of different tokenizer latent spaces , rather than to build state-of-the-art text-to-image generative models or to benchmark fine-grained synthesis. The original paired descriptions in GMAI-VL-5.5M are often long and fine-grained; using them directly may introduce confounding factors from text complexity. We therefore simplify the setup, replacing each caption with a controlled template, e.g. , “A medical {modality} image,” and keep this protocol identical for all tokenizers. Under this setting, differences in generation quality more directly reflect how well each frozen tokenizer organizes medical images into a latent space that is compact, learnable, and amenable to latent diffusion.
blocks.zh:
培训使用来自GMAI-VL-5.5M[1]的70 000个图像,涵盖7个成像模式(每个10 000个图像)。 噪声调度器为DDPM,有1000个时序,一个缩放的线性β调度,和\\epsilon - 预测参数化. 该模型以256个有效批量大小,亚当W优化器,5%线性热能的恒定学习率,以及10%的无分级指导辍学率来进行训练.
请注意,这一实验的目的是比较不同活化剂潜入空间的基因适配性,而不是建立最先进的文本到图像基因模型,或者基准精细的合成. GMAI-VL-5.5M中最初的配对描述往往很长而精细;使用它们会直接引入文本复杂性的混淆因素. 因此,我们简化了设置,将每个标题取而代之的是受控制的模板,例如“医疗{模式}图像”,并且保持对所有标注器相同的协议。 在这种背景下,生成质量的差异更直接地反映了每个被冷冻的活化剂如何将医疗图像组织成一个紧凑、可学习并易于潜在扩散的潜在空间。

blocks.en: We evaluate each frozen tokenizer as a visual backbone within the LLaVA-Med [ 58 ] framework. Given a medical image, the tokenizer encodes it into patch-level tokens, which are then fed through a two-layer MLP connector into Mistral-7B-Instruct as the language model backbone. We train separate LLaVA-Med variants using identical data and hyperparameters while keeping the tokenizer frozen.

blocks.en: Training follows a two-stage protocol. In the first stage, only the MLP connector is trained on approximately 509,369 image–text pairs (learning rate 10 − 3 10^{-3} , one epoch), with 500,000 pairs from PubMedVision [ 66 ] and 9,369 pairs from MM-Skin [ 50 ] . In the second stage, LoRA adapters (rank = = 128, α = \alpha= 256, dropout = = 0.05) are applied to all linear layers of the language model and fine-tuned jointly with the connector (learning rate 10 − 4 10^{-4} for LoRA, 2 × 10 − 5 2{\times}10^{-5} for the connector, one epoch), using 140,151 VQA items for training (70,000 from PubMedVision; 21,778 from the MM-Skin training split; 28,719 from the Kvasir-VQA-x1 training split; 19,654 from the PathVQA training split).

At inference, we use sampling with a temperature of 0.2 0.2 . Model outputs are evaluated via LLM-as-judge binary grading using Qwen3-235B-A22B [ 67 ] . We train each LLaVA-Med variant with three random seeds and report accuracy as mean ± \pm 95% confidence interval in Table 5 .

blocks.en: We compare SliDR with direct gradient matching, total variation (TV), and Laplacian regularization. All variants are initialized from the same 2D-trained MedVTok checkpoint and trained on a controlled subset of 10K volumes. We evaluate volumetric reconstruction on AMOS-MM CT and MRISegmenter MRI (Table 17 ). SliDR achieves the highest mean PSNR and SSIM on both datasets under this setting.

blocks.en: TV and Laplacian regularization penalize first- and second-order depth differences of the reconstructed volume, respectively, without reference to the ground truth. These penalties encourage smoothness even where the input contains genuine inter-slice changes. SliDR instead matches both orders of slice differentials to the ground-truth volume (Eq. 1 ), providing a reconstruction target for anatomical transitions.
blocks.zh: 电视和Laplacian规范化分别惩罚重塑体积的一等和二等深度差异,而不提及地面真相。 即使输入包含真正的切片间变化,这些惩罚也鼓励平滑. 反之,SliDR将两相片相差的顺序相匹配到地真体积(Eq. 1),为解剖过渡提供了重建目标.

blocks.en: To qualitatively assess the discriminative structure of the learned representations, we visualize t t -SNE embeddings of frozen tokenizer features in Fig. 11 . We compare PUMIT, MedVAE, MedITok, and MedVTok on two datasets: (a) a microscopy blood cell dataset PBC [ 68 ] (covering multiple cell types: basophil, eosinophil, erythroblast, immature granulocytes, lymphocyte, monocyte, neutrophil, platelet), which is an out-of-distribution modality not seen during training, and (b) the JSIEC [ 33 ] fundus dataset. On the PBC dataset, MedVTok produces clearly separated clusters for each cell type despite never seeing microscopy images during training, indicating strong generalization of the learned semantic structure. On JSIEC, MedVTok forms tighter, more coherent clusters for fine-grained retinal conditions compared to the baselines, which exhibit more inter-class overlap. These visualizations corroborate the quantitative classification and retrieval results, confirming that MedVTok encodes semantically meaningful representations that generalize across both in-distribution and out-of-distribution modalities.

blocks.en: A general-purpose medical visual tokenizer can accelerate multimodal medical AI research and patient-level modeling by providing a shared, reusable visual interface across imaging modalities. This may lower the barrier for building clinical decision-support tools, particularly for under-resourced specialties or institutions that lack the data and compute. By open-sourcing the model and code, we aim to promote reproducibility and equitable access to medical AI infrastructure.
blocks.zh: 通用医疗视觉标致器可以通过提供跨成像模式的共享,可再利用的视觉界面来加速多模式医疗AI研究和患者级模型. 这可能会降低建立临床决策支持工具的障碍,特别是对于资源不足的专业或缺乏数据和计算的机构而言。 通过开放外包模式和守则,我们的目标是促进可复制性和公平使用医疗AI基础设施。

blocks.en:
As with any medical AI component, there is a risk that downstream systems built on MedVTok could produce incorrect predictions that, if acted upon without appropriate clinical oversight, may lead to patient harm.
We will release MedVTok under the Apache 2.0 license with clear documentation stating that it is intended for research use. We encourage downstream users to rigorously validate performance on their target populations and to comply with applicable regulations before any clinical deployment.
